newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli woman charged over pig posters in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli woman charged over pig posters in Hebron.

text.p: An Israeli woman was charged on Thursday with illegally putting up posters in Hebron depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig and endangering life by stoning an Arab car -- offences that carry a 24-year maximum sentence.

The posters -- pasted last Friday night across 20 storefronts on the Palestinian-ruled side of Hebron -- provoked an outpouring of Moslem Arab anger and a surge in anti-Israeli protests in the volatile West Bank city.

Prosecutors asked the Jerusalem District Court to order that the Jewish woman, Tatyana Suskin of Jerusalem, remain in custody until the end of her trial. A hearing on the request was scheduled for Wednesday.

The charge sheet said she had worn the yellow shirt with a clenched fist symbolic of the outlawed anti-Arab Kach movement of the late Rabbi Meir Kahane when she put up the posters. It said Kahane's name was written across the shirt.

"They don't even let me bring a Torah scroll or prayerbook into jail. They don't let me eat. They do interrogations from morning till night," Suskin, 26, complained to reporters during her court appearance.

The indictment said Suskin hurled a stone at the car of a Palestinian motorist on Saturday, breaking the rear left window and endangering human life on the road -- a charge carrying a maximum 20-year sentence.

Suskin was also charged with harming religious sensitivities, an offence that carries a maximum one-year sentence, and supporting a terrorist group, a charge that carries a maximum three-year sentence.
In Hebron on Thursday, Israeli soldiers posing as Palestinians surprised young Arab protesters and arrested a handful of them who threw stones and burned an Israeli flag outside a Jewish enclave.
The undercover soldiers spoke Arabic, dressed like Palestinians in plain clothes and wore masks and keffiyeh headdresses while mingling with a crowd of about 50 youths.

When the group began hurling stones at uniformed troops and burning an Israeli flag, the undercover men began beating and pushing them, even dragging one along the ground, while making about six arrests, witnesses said.
Troops wounded 37 youths in protests and shot dead an Arab teenager in a clash in Gaza on Wednesday.

"I am sorry to say that they are stepping up their attacks against our people," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters on his return to the self-ruled Gaza Strip from talks in Egypt on the crisis in Middle East peacemaking.

Palestinians are frustrated over a peace process deadlocked since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. But Netanyahu blamed the violence on Arafat's Palestinian Authority.

"This is not spontaneous violence with one or two exceptions. It is organised by the Palestinian Authority and in those cases where it's not organised by the Palestinian Authority, the Palestinian police sit back and do nothing to stop this," Netanyahu told reporters.

Israel Radio said Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai had sent a "sharp message" to the Palestinian Authority, in charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza, cautioning Israel would be forced to use "an iron fist" if the unrest got worse.
But Miguel Angel Moratinos, the European Middle East peace envoy, said he did not believe the Palestinian Authority was behind the violence.
It was unclear how close Netanyahu was to resolving a crisis with his own foreign minister, David Levy, who has threatened to bolt their coalition unless given control over day-to-day peace moves.

Palestinian security sources in Hebron said Ibrahim Ghneimat, a top member of a Hamas military cell that carried out several attacks against Israelis, escaped from a PLO prison in Hebron and police were searching for him.

Ghneimat was among several Hamas guerrillas rounded up by Israel and the Palestinian Authority in April after a bombing in Tel Aviv in March in which three Israeli women were killed. The cell also kidnapped and killed an Israeli soldier.
